why.1: The OUTPUT is only the tail of the document: setpoints SP-24 to SP-38, Appendix B and the pre-issue checks. It refers to Section 5 but contains no step-by-step start sequence. It does not show the slide valve being unloaded before start or the event that begins the 30 s low-oil bypass. OI-06 shows the bypass start point is still open.
why.2: SP-24 and SP-25 give 4 starts per rolling 60-minute window. There is no description of how the limit is enforced or what the operator sees when a start is blocked.
why.3: SP-31 to SP-33 define bad-signal limits and FR-C101-102 tests the HS-130 hardwired circuit with the PLC in PROGRAM mode. Neither states that the 150 ppm shutdown and the ESD cannot be overridden from the HMI. Detector fault behavior for AE-110A/B is not written out in the visible text.
why.4: The pre-issue check says power loss/restart is 'Met (Section 8)', but Section 8 is not in the OUTPUT. No no-auto-restart or latched-trip reset requirement is visible.
why.5: No description of how the current limit interacts with suction pressure control. Only OI-05 (FLA) is mentioned.
why.6: Only the ammonia setpoints are visible, with no delay, action or reset given for them. The oil, discharge temperature and suction trips are not listed with tag, value, delay, action and reset. Sections 6 and 7 are referenced but not included.

why.1: The visible output is only the open-items table and status section. It claims every step has a timeout and failure response, but no startup steps, completion criteria or timeouts are shown (e.g., for failing to reach 500 rpm or an interrupted hold).
why.2: Nothing in the output says the 1600-1900 rpm band cannot be held, or what happens on an operator hold or a stall in the band. OI-05 only asks whether the vibration trip changes inside the band.
why.3: There is no coastdown description. OI-06 and OI-11 mention M-15 engagement and P-12 hardwired start logic only as open questions, and FR-ST1-305 suggests M-15 stops on low oil. Oil availability, DC backup during coastdown and turning-gear engagement at zero speed are not specified.
why.4: OI-04 defers the decision on which device executes each trip (Woodward or independent trip system). Overspeed protection is not explicitly allocated to the governor or hardwired protection anywhere in the visible text.
why.5: Trip reset requirements (latching, conditions to reset) are not shown, nor is the requirement that a restart after a trip goes back through the permissives. OI-10 only mentions sequence-of-events resolution for first-out.
why.6: The open-items table flags many items for confirmation rather than inventing values: cold-start criterion and warm/hot M-15 run time (OI-02), the hold-applicability assumption (OI-03), voting choices (OI-04), vibration measurement basis and behavior in the critical band (OI-05), M-15 engagement (OI-06), and SP-34 left TBD pending OEM data.

why.1: The visible output lists only cascade parameters (DO_OUT_A1 30%, DO_OUT_A2 70%, DO_SAT_TIME, SIC530 80–140 rpm). It never states when agitation hands over to air or air to O2, or how stages hand back.
why.2: Thresholds (PH_PROBE_DEV, DO_PROBE_DEV with delays) and alarms (AL-11, AL-12) are given. What the controller uses when one probe is bad or the probes disagree is only referenced (FR-BR500-102 to 104, IL-05/06, DO HOLD) and never actually defined in the visible text.
why.3: BASE_WARN is 32 L, before the limit. P-520 stops at BASE_LIMIT minus BASE_STOP_MARGIN, and the stop latches until the next batch with no operator reset. The base total survives restart. This is close to the expectation, though reset at batch start is only implied by 'until the next batch'.
why.4: It says only that Hold, Stop and Abort do not disable control, and leaves that as an open item. It gives no behaviour on transition into Harvest and no final state of the valves, pump and agitator at end of control.
why.5: No visible statement addresses CO2 sparge affecting dissolved gas or any interaction or limit between the pH and DO loops.
why.6: A system prompt for reason entry (SEQ-2), a reason list, a record-write-failure alarm and batch-record persistence are present. The required record fields (user, time, old and new value) are not specified in the visible text.

why.1: Section 4 splits DO demand into three stages with defined breakpoints: DO_S1_END=40% and DO_S2_END=70%, each with its actuator range. FR-BR500-017 requires SIC-530 to reach AGIT_MAX before FCV-511 opens, and FCV-511 to reach AIR_MAX before FCV-512 opens. FR-BR500-018 reverses that order on falling demand with an AGIT_MIN floor. FR-BR500-019 adds a rate limit.
why.2: Disagreement thresholds are defined: PH_PRB_DEV 0.10 pH and DO_PRB_DEV 10%, each with a delay. Alarms AL-04/AL-15 cover disagreement. FR-BR500-044 says control continues on the average and prompts PR-02 for probe selection. FR-BR500-039/041 use the healthy probe when one is bad, with AL-05/AL-16. IL-04/IL-05 handle both bad.
why.3: AL-08 warns at BASE_WARN (32 L). IL-01 trips at BASE_LIM minus BASE_MARGIN, stops P-520, blocks Manual start, latches through power loss and raises AL-09. The base total resets only on a new batch ID (FR-BR500-007, IL-01 reset), and SEQ-1 initializes it at start.
why.4: Hold: loops and outputs continue unchanged. Abort: immediate safe state with FCV-510 and FCV-512 closed, P-520 off, and FCV-511 and SIC-530 released at their last value. Harvest: loops go Out of service via Complete and SEQ-2, which defines the final valve, pump and agitator states.
why.5: No requirement states the effect of CO2 sparge on dissolved gas or DO, or any limit between the pH and DO loops. Only open item OI-10 mentions assessing CO2 stripping by air sparge and total gas flow, which defers the issue rather than specifying it. IL-07 covers acid/base interaction only.
why.6: FR-BR500-022 and SEQ-4 enforce a system prompt (PR-04) with a mandatory reason. Without a reason the change is cancelled. The system writes a record with batch ID, phase, parameter, old value, new value, time, user and reason before applying the change, and keeps the old value if the write fails.

why.1: The output is a truncated tail (sections 10-12) and contains no staging criteria, thresholds, delays, or minimum on/off times; staging is only referenced indirectly (SP IDs, OI-02/OI-09 'staging logic' still to settle).
why.2: No minimum flow control logic using FCV-701 and FIT-702 is shown; FIT-702 appears only in an open item about piping location, and staging-transition flow behavior is not defined.
why.3: Prompt P-01 states 'CH-n tripped. The standby chiller started' and references SEQ-D, implying auto-start with alarm, but the actual sequence including pump and tower sequencing is not present in the output.
why.4: Only OI-05 mentions confirming humidity limits for the 'CHWST reset hold (FR-CHW-024)'; the reset hold/limit logic based on critical valve position is not defined in the output.
why.5: No BAS controller or network failure behavior is described; P-05 covers power-loss restart only, and OI-04 defers restart behavior to the vendor.
why.6: Only 'chiller start order and maintenance flag' as operator-changeable items; no rotation criteria (runtime, schedule) or requirement that rotation not drop running capacity.

why.1: The OUTPUT is only a sign-off, change log, and pre-issue check section. It refers to a setpoint list and Table R, but no actual values with units for heat-up rate, fuel changeover temperature, or feed start conditions appear, and no value is shown marked as from-notes versus to-confirm.
why.2: There is not enough content to judge. The OUTPUT says values are 'marked confirm', but it shows no aux-drive rotation schedule or feed ramp values, flagged or otherwise. Nothing in the OUTPUT itself demonstrates the expectation.
why.3: I-01/I-02 are mentioned only as items awaiting LOPA classification. The OUTPUT gives no CO alarm or trip value, delay, ESP de-energize action, or reset logic.
why.4: The checklist only claims power loss/restart is 'Met'. The OUTPUT contains no requirement for an aux drive on an independent power source, and no trigger or operator actions.
why.5: The only ID fan item is that its damper fails open (OI-15). Nothing defines the ID fan minimum as an enforced limit while firing, and the OUTPUT does not show automatic actions separated from operator actions.
why.6: The OUTPUT cites OI-01 to OI-17 and says they have owners and dates, but the questions themselves are not listed. Only OI-02, OI-04, OI-07 and OI-15 are named, briefly. Referring to the list is not the same as listing the open questions.

why.1: The visible output shows only the open-items table and closing checks. It refers to SP/RT/TO IDs but shows no actual heat-up rate, changeover temperature, or feed-start values with units. It also does not visibly mark which values came from the notes versus which need confirmation.
why.2: OI-01 requires every value in the setpoint, rotation, and timer lists to be confirmed with the senior operator. OI-06 flags the RT-1 to RT-4 rotation intervals as to be confirmed, and OI-07 flags the feed-ramp speed profile as undefined. Vague items are therefore flagged rather than presented as settled.
why.3: Only an open item is visible: confirm SP-018 to SP-020 and TO-019 with the ESP supplier. No CO alarm or trip value, delay, ESP de-energize action, or reset logic is shown in the output.
why.4: OI-05 only asks to confirm the emergency power source for M-KLN-102 and define a backup turning method. The checks mention that power loss is in section 8, but no requirement with an independent power source, trigger, or operator actions is visible.
why.5: SP-007 is mentioned only as an unclear value (fan speed or damper position). No enforced ID fan minimum interlock while firing is visible, and there is no visible split between automatic actions and operator actions.
why.6: A detailed open-items table (OI-01 to OI-12) assigns owners and dates to the gaps. Examples include the tower-hot definition, precalciner firing, hot restart, and dry-out curve. It also explicitly lists which items need the retiring operator.
